## EVIDENCE for the final two criteria — harness run 30951453979, and the assertion checked for vacuity

Both remaining criteria are met. The run is `30951453979` (`Live External Integration`, main @
`d394a70529`, DC harness job 40m09s, **3 failed / 59 passed / 1 xfailed**).

### The evidence line printed, for every provisioned project

    [2e47-issue-type-evidence] project RBJREXN offers ['Bug', 'Epic', 'Story', 'Sub-task', 'Task'];
      instance-wide entries matching ['Task', 'Sub-task', 'Epic']
      (GET /rest/api/2/issuetype -> HTTP 200): [('10002', 'Task'), ('10003', 'Sub-task'), ('10000', 'Epic')]

The 1390 fix worked: the line is now unconditional and reads `/rest/api/2/issuetype` (the earlier
version filtered `/rest/api/2/field` against issue-type NAMES, so it could never match and silently
never printed).

### Criterion 1 — the duplicate `Task` ambiguity does NOT reach the project scheme

**I did not take the printed list as the proof, because it cannot be.** The project-offered half is
rendered `sorted(set(offered_names))`, so a duplicate would COLLAPSE in the display. I checked the
producing code (`tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py:499-534`) before concluding:

    offered_names = [ ... ]                                              # a LIST
    ambiguous = sorted({n for n in offered_names if offered_names.count(n) > 1})
    if ambiguous: raise AssertionError("PROVISIONING FAILED: ... MORE THAN ONCE ...")

The duplicate check runs `count(...) > 1` over the **list**, not the deduped set — so it is NOT
vacuous, and the `set()` appears only in the print. This mattered enough to verify because bug 59b2
in this same epic was exactly a family of vacuous assertions.

The assertion lives in the provisioning fixture, so **a run that executes tests at all is the
evidence**: 62 tests ran across many scratch projects, therefore `ambiguous` was empty for every one.
The instance-wide inventory shows one id per required name on this image
(`10002`/`10003`/`10000`). Instance-wide duplicates are deliberately REPORTED, not asserted —
failing on them would refuse a project that is perfectly usable — which is the "documented as
harmless with evidence" branch the criterion offers. Resolving types by ID is therefore unnecessary.

### Criterion 2 — the declared contract fails loudly on a future instance change

Satisfied by the same assertion (landed in 1381): it raises `PROVISIONING FAILED` naming the
offending name(s), so an image whose project scheme starts offering a duplicate cannot run silently.

### Also re-confirmed in this run: the label-ceiling retraction was RIGHT

`test_the_instance_label_ceiling_measured_at_254_and_255` FAILED in run 30944241768 and **PASSES
here**, after 1389 corrected the assertion to 255-accepted. Positive confirmation that the capability
map's req-0071/0072/0073 entry did not reproduce and the shared constant was correct all along.
[rebar:2c93-ce1c-127e-4d58] is left to record the per-deployment question, now largely moot.

### Not this ticket's failures

The run's 3 remaining failures are all DC parent/hierarchy cells
(`inbound_set_subtask_parent`, `outbound_set_subtask_parent`, `outbound_clear_parent`) — unrelated to
vocabularies, never passing in any of 12 harness runs, and now tracked by
[rebar:9f26-66c2-14af-4223] and [rebar:4b9e-bcad-456a-4233]. Closing this ticket does not paper over
them.

Closing `--class env_integration`: the findings were instance-vocabulary mismatches, one of which
(the label ceiling) did not reproduce at all.
